parsed.explanation: The dossier documents state-tolerated, patterned targeting that explicitly includes trans women: arbitrary detention, prosecution under Article 120 (up to 3 years, applied through 2023), forced examinations meeting the WHO torture definition, and persistent impunity. Routine police extortion (pay or be arrested) and coerced informing add a continuous shakedown exposure. No anti-discrimination law exists; the 2023 constitution deliberately omits sexual orientation; LGBTI organisations cannot register; official hostility is on record, with an unverified proposed discussion ban. No operative remedy for a trans visitor is documented. Entry rules, facilities, care and trans-specific killing figures are absent — unknown, not safe. No execution pathway is documented, keeping this above the 0.15 band's worst cases, but torture-in-custody plus impunity plus routine extortion anchors it near the 0.20 boundary.

entry_documents.exposure: Entry, visa, document-marker and airport-screening treatment of gender-nonconforming travellers are explicitly unaddressed by any source in this inventory.
entry_documents.interaction: Border friction is unknown; any outing there would feed into the documented police apparatus rather than a protective screening regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police arbitrarily detain, prosecute and imprison gay/bisexual men and trans women; forced examinations in these cases meet the WHO torture definition; arrest or threat of arrest is used to extract bribes and coerce informing, with impunity for ill-treatment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented safeguard; remedies for custody abuse are not shown to operate.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any stop for document or presentation mismatch routes the visitor into this custody regime, where torture and extortion are patterned, not incidental.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: All criminal and enforcement provisions are national and uniform; no subnational variation is measured. Facility, ward and cell-placement rules for trans people are unaddressed.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Uniform national policing means no safer region exists to travel within; custody placement rules remain an open question stacked on documented torture in custody.

care_services.exposure: Access to gender-affirming care, medication continuity and emergency-care discrimination are not addressed; criminalisation of HIV transmission appears only as a report scope, not a finding.
care_services.interaction: An illness or injury requiring disclosure would expose the visitor to the same hostile police apparatus, since outed trans people are documented police targets.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official hostility: April 2023 constitution deliberately omits sexual orientation while listing gender, race, religion, nationality; LGBTI organisations cannot register; an unverified November 2024 proposal would ban LGBTQ discussion; police describe LGBTQI people as extortion and informing targets.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Only external UN advocacy urging decriminalisation; Article 120 remained in force as of July 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing licence and directs street-level policing, converting ordinary encounters into detention, forced examination or bribe demands.

minors_guardians.exposure: No source addresses travel with a minor, parental treatment, or child-welfare intervention involving a trans parent or guardian.
minors_guardians.interaction: A accompanying child would be present during any documented stop, detention or extortion episode, but no minor-specific consequence is evidenced; extrapolation only.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Discrimination, violence, blackmail and extortion from both state and non-state actors with almost no legal protection (2021 monitor); continuing societal harassment (2023); rural taboos drive discrimination; impunity for police ill-treatment persists.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; no anti-discrimination law exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Societal hostility and police predation reinforce each other, so calling police after an assault risks entering the extortion/detention pipeline instead of obtaining protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no constitutional anchor on sexual orientation, unregistered LGBTI groups, no documented functioning complaint channel for visitors; censorship self-practice narrows locally available information.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Whether the constitution's listed 'gender' covers gender identity is unresolved; no operative remedy for a trans visitor is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Hostile institutions are the enforcing actor, so efficient rule of law compounds rather than mitigates exposure; unknowns (entry rules, facilities, care, trans killings) cannot be read as safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.15-A, custody abuse (forced examinations amounting to torture) is documented and remedies are shown to fail — police ill-treatment enjoys impunity. Lower than 0.15-A because no months-long pretrial pattern, coerced-confession prosecution machinery, or capital provision tied to presentation is documented here; imprisonment tops out at three years.

Shares routine detention, photographic recording and bribe extraction with open files, and slow or absent relief. Lower than 0.25-A because torture in custody is documented as a definitional finding, prosecution under a live statute runs through 2023, the constitution actively withholds protection, and no court overturning of convictions appears — 0.25-A's courts at least annul some cases.

Matches 0.35-B's pattern of stops, confiscation and compelled interviews with nominal complaint procedures. Higher than 0.35-B because here detention escalates to documented torture-grade forced examinations with impunity and criminal prosecution up to three years, not mere hours-long release, placing this case a full band lower.

Like 0.45-D, the visitor is durably exposed through routine official contact with no credible lethal endpoint. Higher than 0.45-D because that anchor's harms are administrative (registration, eviction, interviews) with uncommon custody, whereas here arrest, torture in custody and extortion are documented police practice against trans women specifically.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a single, uniform national system in which the state itself is the primary threat. Article 120 is live and applied, and police explicitly target trans women alongside gay men — arbitrary detention, forced examinations meeting the torture definition, bribe extortion and coerced informing, all with impunity. Outing probability is raised by this being universal-exposure policing rather than locality-dependent: there is no documented safer region. Societal harassment and rural taboo layer onto state predation, while the constitution's deliberate omission of sexual orientation, absent anti-discrimination law and unregistrable LGBTI organisations leave no operative remedy for a visitor. Entry, facility, care and killing-rate questions are open unknowns and cannot be credited as safety. No execution pathway is documented, which separates this from the 0.05–0.15 floor; routine torture-grade custody and total recourse failure keep it near the bottom of the High Risk band. Travelling with a minor adds no documented specific exposure but places a child inside the same undocumented custody episode.
